us.headline: Tariff stacks and origin rules — not mill prices — drive your landed cost. New tariff measures now in effect.

regulation.b: China-origin goods carry additive Section 301 duties (many lists 25%; consumer List 4A 7.5%). USTR's second four-year review is underway — comment windows on the 2018 actions run through summer 2026 (the 23 Aug 2018 action window opens 24 Jun 2026) — and current product exclusions run only to 9 Nov 2026. New U.S. import tariffs are now in effect as of early August, potentially impacting a broader range of goods. Origin and HTS classification materially change landed cost; confirm each item's status before costing. The effective tariff rate on Chinese goods was 29.3% as of November 2025.
Duties compose additively (MFN + Section 301 + any Section 232 on steel/aluminium). Confirm each product's HTS code before costing.

us.supply: On the Transpacific trade route, spot rates from Shanghai to New York rose 10% to $8,706 per 40ft container, while rates from Shanghai to Los Angeles increased 6% to $6,244 per 40ft container. Carriers are actively restricting space by utilising blank sailings. Meanwhile, port congestion across Asian ports following typhoon Dolphin and low-water conditions in the Rhine river continued to constrain capacity, providing further support to freight rates on certain lanes. Brent crude stands elevated around $89.16 USD per barrel due to ongoing regional instability and the severe disruption of the Strait of Hormuz, keeping resin and energy-linked input costs highly volatile, though polypropylene resin prices are softening.
us.view: US landed cost is dominated by tariffs and origin, not spot material prices. New tariff measures are now in effect, adding significant uncertainty. Birdland's two-country production (Taiwan + China) lets you shift origin to manage tariff exposure, and we prepare clear origin documentation. With Transpacific freight now sharply up (NY up 10%, LA up 6%), strategic booking is advised — our pricing reflects secured capacity and compliant origin, not a single day's index. Elevated Brent crude suggests locking fuel-linked inputs.

summary.changed: Transpacific freight rates have sharply increased (NY up 10%, LA up 6%), and Brent crude remains elevated at $89.16/bbl.
summary.action: Strategically book ocean freight capacity immediately and lock in fuel-linked inputs to mitigate rising costs.

ca.headline: ‘Country of melt’ now decides whether China steel surtaxes hit you. Brent crude remains elevated.

regulation.b: Since 31 Jul 2025 Canada applies a 25% surtax on steel melted & poured (and aluminium cast) in China, on top of normal duties. From 26 Dec 2025 a 25% tariff also covers listed steel-derivative products — some with only partial steel content. The surtax regime has been extended to June 27, 2027.

Several temporary remissions narrowed from 1 Jul 2026 — now in effect — including the end of relief for aluminium, public-health/safety goods, and motor-vehicle and aircraft inputs, though the Steel Derivative Goods Surtax Remission Order (Feb 2026; CBSA guidance Mar 2026) keeps category-based relief for a defined list, extended to June 30, 2027 for some auto and aerospace inputs.

ca.supply: Landed steel cost into Canada is shaped more by origin-of-melt surtaxes than by mill prices. ca.view: Birdland can source Taiwan-melted steel content with clear traceability, helping you stay outside the China-melt surtax, and we document origin end-to-end. Brent crude stands elevated around $89.16 USD per barrel due to ongoing regional instability and the severe disruption of the Strait of Hormuz, keeping resin and energy-linked input costs highly volatile. eu.view: As an EU destination, Europe rewards suppliers who arrive compliance-ready. Birdland prepares EUDR geolocation and legal-timber evidence, supports CBAM carbon data on steel parts, and reviews coatings against PPWR PFAS limits — while strategically booking freight and locking key materials. When costs dip, the honest takeaway is not “cut price” but “lock stability before the next swing”: our quotes reflect secured materials, compliant documentation and reliable supply, not yesterday’s spot price.

teamAnalysis: Compliance and origin remain primary drivers of landed cost, overshadowing spot prices. EU buyers face tightening EUDR, CBAM (with Q2 2026 certificate price now EUR 81.91 per tonne), and the application of PPWR PFAS limits from August 12, 2026, with EUDR implementation deadlines holding firm despite IT system challenges. US and Canadian costs are shaped by tariff stacks and country-of-origin/melt rules, with new US tariff measures now in effect. Ocean freight trends are mixed, with Transpacific rates sharply increasing (NY up 10%, LA up 6%) while Asia-Europe rates are softening. Brent crude remains elevated around $89.16 USD per barrel due to the severe disruption of the Strait of Hormuz and geopolitical risks, though polypropylene resin prices continue to soften. These market dynamics reinforce the importance of securing supply, capacity, and robust documentation early. Birdland's two-country production model, proactive freight booking, strategic material locking, and comprehensive compliance paperwork ensure stable supply and protect your margins amidst ongoing volatility.

expert: 對台灣出口:鋼與電鍍/包材偏漲,鋼質手工具到岸成本壓力升,建議分批鎖鋼料、優化包材規格。
對中國出口:木材與樹膠走軟有利木柄/握把成本,但 EUDR(木材)合規文件成關鍵門檻。
綜合:成本結構分散,維持台灣+中國雙基地調度,用『鎖料+文件齊備』把波動轉成穩定供應的賣點。

shipping_bot.simple: 海運成本像搭車的車資——歐洲線塞車漲價、美西順暢降價;港口和拖車的『小費』也在變。
expert: 對台灣/中國出口:歐洲線運價與旺季附加偏漲,建議提前訂艙、鎖長約;美西回軟可保留彈性。
內陸拖運與海關倉儲/查驗成本上升,出貨節奏與文件齊備能直接省下滯港與查驗成本。
綜合:把運費波動納入報價(BAF/PSS 先估),用提前佈局把不確定變可預期,是對客戶最有價值的服務。

reg_bot.simple: 法規像考試規則一直在改——歐美越來越看『木材哪來的、鋼的碳排多少、有沒有強迫勞動』,文件不齊就卡關。
expert: 對台灣出口:CBAM(鋼)、EUDR(木)文件成歐洲市場門檻;台灣熔煉鋼還能規避加拿大附加稅,是優勢。
對中國出口:原產地查驗趨嚴 + 美 UFLPA,『中國製』暴露於關稅與審查,雙基地調度與產地文件是關鍵。
綜合:把『合規文件齊備』做成標準服務,等於替客戶清掉通關風險,是最強的差異化。
